Folks — adding some technical notes ahead of the sync that should address the major asks from Acme: 

- Shadowing approach: Redwood will propose to create customer‑scoped shadow FQDNs in the pattern <service>.<customer>.priv.redwood.ai, mapped to Acme on‑prem IPs via the attached CSV. If Acme prefers delegated subzones (e.g., tenant.acme.internal), we can support NS delegation but that requires zone transfer allowances from your DNS team.

- Certificate delivery: We will push cert bundles (leaf+intermediates) to the on‑prem provisioning agent over mTLS. The agent will write to the local cert store and trigger a rolling restart of the sidecar/edge as configured. Our pipeline supports OCSP stapling for leaf certs and will publish stapling responses when termination is on Redwood proxies.

- Termination options:
  * Edge termination (recommended for minimal changes): Redwood edge proxy terminates TLS, SNI maps to upstream service IPs. Requires explicit SNI mapping and a shared CA pin for validation of backend.
  * Sidecar termination (preferred for maximal end‑to‑end encryption): sidecars present client certs to upstream services; requires mutual TLS and a rotation plan for client certs.

- Rotation windows: Karthik confirms we can orchestrate a 72h soft overlap by default; we can tighten to 48h for critical endpoints as requested.

Action items I can take before the call:
- Produce a minimal SNI mapping template (CSV) and an example zone delegation snippet.
- Run a compatibility check for OCSP stapling and report which of the proposed leaf CAs support stapling across our edge fleet.
